A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RaNA research work. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1-A.4, are available and readable, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Llama2-7b, Gemma-2b, and Pythia models, including accuracy, perplexity, reconstruction errors, latency, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A, including the benchmark comparisons and component ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Appendix A.4 retain identical RaNA decompositions, maskers, neuron thresholding, FLOP-allocation procedures, and Algorithms 1-3.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama and the Pile, with downstream evaluations on HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and RACE. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain CATS and, for Llama2-7b, SliceGPT. Figure 3 retains the same experiment-specific CATS, SVD, Neuron-Adaptive, and LLRA comparisons; appendix comparator membership also matches.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same models, fine-tuning budgets, zero-shot/five-shot settings, evaluation metrics, sequence lengths, and latency procedure. Appendix ablation settings and compression configurations also match.

E4.justification: The rank-contribution sparsity and layer-reconstruction analyses are unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the same QKV-compression and FLOP-allocation ablations and SliceGPT trade-off comparison.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, with no added or revised repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: All results in Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-4 match. For example, Table 1 retains RaNA's 56.37% average accuracy and 8.04 perplexity at 42% FLOP compression; Table 3 retains ablation perplexities of 8.40, 8.79, and 9.10.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, optimization objectives, Proposition 1 and its proof, Theorem 1, and the theorem's proof in Appendix A.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about generalizing neuron adaptation, supporting MLP and QKV layers, and improving accuracy, perplexity, and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations based on adaptive compression and FLOP allocation, Appendix A.2's static-versus-adaptive compression trade-off, and Section 6's applicability boundaries and future directions are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code link, decomposition sample count, fine-tuning details, NVIDIA L40S hardware disclosure, masked GEMV implementation, compression breakdown, and appendix pseudocode are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Added arXiv labels and identifiers describe existing references, including LoRA and LLM-Pruner; they do not introduce new works or revise the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 expands existing bibliography entries with arXiv preprint metadata and updates the first-page version/date stamp. The main prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography additions alter typography, line wrapping, spacing, and the split of the Gemma reference across pages 12-13. All figures, tables, algorithm displays, and scientific-page layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes existing references more explicit through bibliographic metadata and modest reformatting. The scientific exposition, proofs, experimental evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain identical, including the appendices. This editorial cleanup does not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
